_comment: Extra editorial content for game pages: strategy tips and a short FAQ. Keyed by game slug. Keep every statement consistent with the game's own rules in games.json.

tips: Count both routes before every turn. If your shortest path is already shorter than your rival's, moving is usually better than forging.
Save blocks for the endgame. A single block placed when your rival is two steps from their goal can add several moves to their route.
Place blocks where they force a long detour, such as next to an existing wall, rather than in open space where the runner simply steps around.
Spark cells are worth a short detour early in the game, because every extra block becomes more valuable later.
Use the H key to show your shortest path and check that a block you are about to forge really lengthens your rival's route.
faq: Can I trap my rival completely?
No. A block that would cut off every route to a goal is not allowed, and those cells are not highlighted. You can only make the route longer.
What does vaulting do?
When your rival stands directly next to you and the cell behind them is free, you can jump straight over them. It is a quick way to get past a runner who is blocking a corridor.
How do I play with a friend?
Choose the two-player mode and take turns on the same device. Cyan heads for the top row and magenta for the bottom row.

tips: Stay near the middle of the arena. It gives you room to escape in every direction when bars and shards arrive together.
Watch for the flashing laser warning and move away early. Waiting until the last moment gets harder as the game speeds up.
Only chase an energy core when the path to it is clear. A +50 bonus is not worth ending the run.
Make small, controlled movements. Big sweeps across the arena often steer you straight into the next obstacle.
Pause with P or Esc if you need a break. The pace rises every 15 seconds, so a fresh focus helps on long runs.
faq: How is the score calculated?
Your score grows every second you survive, and each energy core you collect adds a 50-point bonus.
Does the game get harder?
Yes. The speed increases every 15 seconds, so obstacles arrive faster the longer you last.
Is my best score saved?
Yes. Your personal best is stored in your browser on this device.

tips: Pick a target colour early. Usually the colour that already covers most of the board is the cheapest one to finish with.
Remember that every tap changes five tiles: the one you tap and its four neighbours. Corner and edge tiles change fewer tiles, which makes them useful for small fixes.
Work row by row. Fixing the top rows first and pushing the remaining differences downward keeps the board easier to read.
Tapping the same tile repeatedly cycles it around the whole colour wheel, so sometimes going 'past' a colour is the shortest route.
Try a level once without hints. A hint helps when you are stuck, but it limits that level to two stars.
faq: Do I have to match a particular colour?
No. Any colour counts, as long as every tile on the board ends up the same.
How do stars work?
Clearing a level within the move limit completes it, and using fewer moves earns more stars. Using a hint caps the level at two stars.
Can I play if I find some colours hard to tell apart?
Yes. Every colour has its own symbol, so you can solve every level by symbol alone.

tips: Look at the rows furthest up the screen, not the car right in front of you. At high speed you need to pick your gap early.
Avoid zig-zagging across all four lanes. Moving one lane at a time keeps you in control and makes the next gap easier to reach.
Near misses are worth +5 each, so passing close to cars in the next lane adds up, but only take them when the lane ahead is clear.
Coins are worth +25. Collect them when they sit in your planned lane, and skip ones that force a risky swerve.
Each difficulty keeps its own best score, so practise reading traffic on an easier level before chasing a record on the hardest one.
faq: Is there always a way through the traffic?
Yes. Every row of traffic leaves at least one gap that you can reach.
How is my score worked out?
Your score is the distance you drive in metres plus bonuses: +25 for each coin and +5 for each near miss.
Does the car get faster?
Yes. Your speed keeps increasing the longer you drive, which is what makes long runs difficult.

tips: Use the edges of the paddle to aim. Hitting the ball off-centre sends it sideways, which is the best way to reach bricks behind steel blocks.
Try to get the ball above the bricks. Once it is bouncing between the top wall and the bricks it clears many of them without you touching it.
Prioritise the multi-ball and slower-ball power-ups when several fall at once. Extra balls clear levels fast, and a slower ball buys you time.
Do not chase every power-up. Losing your last ball while reaching for one costs a life.
Steel bricks never break, so plan angles around them instead of hitting them repeatedly.
faq: What do the brick colours mean?
Orange bricks break in one hit, yellow in two and red in three. Grey steel bricks never break, and green bricks always drop a power-up.
What do the power-ups do?
W makes the paddle wider, M adds two extra balls, S slows the ball down and the heart gives an extra life, up to five lives.
How do I finish a level?
Clear every breakable brick. Steel bricks do not need to be broken.

tips: Wait for fruit to bunch together near the top of its arc, then slice several in one quick swipe to build your combo.
Your combo can reach x5, so a single swipe through five pieces scores far more than five separate slices.
Keep your swipes short and deliberate when bombs are on screen. Hitting one costs five seconds and resets your combo.
Star fruit is worth three points before the multiplier, so include it in combos whenever you can.
Bombs appear more often later in the round, so take more risks in the first half and play carefully near the end.
faq: How long is a round?
Each round lasts 60 seconds. Hitting a bomb takes five seconds off the clock.
How do combos work?
Slice fruit in quick succession: the second piece scores double, the third triple, and so on up to five times.
Is my best score saved?
Yes. Your best score is stored in your browser on this device.

tips: Pick one weapon and keep collecting it. Grabbing the same pick-up again upgrades it, up to level 3.
The pulse cannon pierces through enemies, which makes it strong against lines of drones and armoured tanks.
Stay low on the screen and move sideways to dodge. You have more time to react to zig-zaggers' shots from further away.
Save shields and repair kits for boss waves when you can. Every fifth wave is a boss, and it changes its attack when its health drops below half.
Avoid heavy hits: they can knock a level off your weapon, so dodging well also protects your firepower.
faq: Do I have to keep pressing fire?
No. Auto-fire is on by default. You can turn it off on the title screen or with F, and then fire with Space.
What do the pick-up letters mean?
B is the rapid blaster, S the wide spread gun, P the piercing pulse cannon, + is a repair kit and O is a shield.
When do bosses appear?
Every fifth wave. When a boss's health bar falls below half, it switches to a second attack pattern.

tips: Flip cards in a fixed order, row by row, so it is easier to remember where each symbol was.
When you turn over a new card, check whether you have already seen its match before flipping a random second card.
Say the symbol and its position to yourself, for example 'star, top left'. Naming things helps memory.
Start with the Easy 4×3 board to learn a system, then move up to Medium and Hard.
In two-player games, remember the cards your friend reveals too. Their misses are free information for you.
faq: How is the solo score calculated?
Fewer moves and a faster time give a higher score. Finishing within the move target earns three stars.
How does two-player mode work?
Players take turns on one device. Finding a pair earns a point and another turn; a miss passes the turn. Whoever finds the most pairs wins.
How big are the boards?
Easy is 4×3 with 6 pairs, Medium is 4×4 with 8 pairs and Hard is 6×5 with 15 pairs.

tips: If you move first, take the centre or a corner. Both give you the most ways to make three in a row.
Always check whether your opponent can win on their next move, and block it before going for your own line.
Look for a 'fork': a move that creates two possible winning lines at once. Your opponent can only block one of them.
When your opponent takes a corner first, answering in the centre is the safest reply.
Against Hard, the computer plays perfectly. A draw means you made no mistakes.
faq: Can I beat the Hard computer?
No. Hard plays perfectly and never loses, so a draw is the best possible result.
Who goes first?
The first move alternates every round, so both players get the same number of starts.
How do I play with a friend online?
Create a private room, send your friend the 6-character code or invite link, and both press Ready. The host then starts the game, and the server checks every move.

tips: Keep your snake moving along the walls in long loops when it gets big. It leaves open space in the middle and avoids tight turns.
Plan an escape route before you grab food in a corner, especially as the snake gets longer.
Gold bonus food is worth +50 points but adds three segments at once, so make sure you have room before taking it.
The snake speeds up every four meals. Practise on relaxed speed to learn safe paths before trying classic or fast.
Use pause (P, Space or Esc) to look at the board when the arena is crowded.
faq: What ends the game?
Hitting a wall or any part of your own body. You cannot turn straight back into yourself.
How do points work?
Each normal meal is worth 10 points and adds one segment. Every fifth meal a gold bonus appears for a few seconds, worth 50 points and three segments.
Are scores saved for each speed?
Yes. Relaxed, classic and fast each keep their own best score on your device.

tips: Keep your highest tile in one corner and build the rest of the row next to it in descending order.
Mainly use two or three directions. Pressing the fourth direction often pulls your big tile out of its corner.
Keep at least one row or column full so it does not slide unexpectedly when you move.
Think one move ahead about where the new 2 or 4 might appear, and avoid leaving a single empty cell next to your big tiles.
Save your three undos for real mistakes late in the game, when one bad move can end a long run.
faq: What happens when I reach 2048?
You win the game, and you can keep playing afterwards to push your score higher.
How is the score calculated?
Every time two tiles fuse, the value of the new tile is added to your score.
Will I lose my game if I close the page?
No. An unfinished game is saved on your device so you can continue later.

tips: Watch the block's rhythm for one or two passes before tapping. Timing a regular movement is easier than reacting to it.
Tap when the block is directly above the tower, not when it is about to arrive. Your reaction time adds a small delay.
Aim for perfect drops: they keep your width and three in a row make your block wider again.
When your block becomes narrow, focus on safe drops rather than perfect ones. Any overlap keeps the game going.
The blocks speed up as the tower grows, so stay calm and keep a steady tapping rhythm.
faq: What counts as a perfect drop?
A block that lands almost exactly on top of the one below. It keeps the full width and earns a streak bonus of up to +5.
How can I make my block wider again?
Land three perfect drops in a row.
When does the game end?
When a block misses the tower completely.

tips: Aim for bubbles that hold up large groups. Popping them makes everything below fall for +20 per bubble.
Use the side walls for bank shots. The dotted guide shows exactly where a bounced shot will travel.
Swap your current bubble with the next one when the current colour has no good target.
Watch the shot counter: five shots in a row without a pop lower the ceiling, so do not waste shots near the red line.
Save bomb bubbles for dense clusters, and use rainbow bubbles to complete a group that is one bubble short.
faq: When does the game end?
When any bubble reaches the red line at the bottom of the board.
What do the special bubbles do?
A bomb bubble pops everything it touches. A rainbow bubble takes the colour of the first bubble it touches.
Can I play if I find some colours hard to tell apart?
Yes. Every colour also has its own symbol.

tips: Drive slowly. Small, controlled movements make it much easier to line up with the bay.
Remember the car turns with its front wheels. Swing wide before a turn so the back of the car clears corners and other cars.
Use reverse to straighten up. A short reverse with the wheels turned can fix a crooked approach.
For parallel parking, stop beside the bay, reverse with full steering, then straighten the wheels as the car slides in.
Get a clean finish first, then replay a level to beat the par time for three stars.
faq: How do I complete a level?
Drive into the green bay marked P, line the car up with it and stop. Hold still for a moment to finish.
What fails a level?
Touching a wall, a barrier or another car. Press R or Retry to start again instantly.
Can every level be solved?
Yes. Every level has been checked by an automatic solver to make sure it can be completed.

tips: In the opening, control the centre with your pawns and develop your knights and bishops before moving the same piece twice.
Castle early to keep your king safe and connect your rooks.
Before every move, check which of your pieces are attacked and which are undefended.
Tap a piece to see its legal moves. It is an easy way to spot captures and checks you might otherwise miss.
Start against the casual computer and move up to normal and strong as your play improves.
faq: Are all the official rules included?
Yes: castling, en passant, promotion to any piece, check, checkmate, stalemate, and draws by threefold repetition, the 50-move rule and insufficient material.
How does undo work against the computer?
Undo takes back your last move and the computer's reply, so it is your turn again.
Can I play chess with a friend online?
Yes. Create a private room and share the code or invite link. Colours swap every game, and you can offer a draw or resign.
